title: Word Seesaw: testing the fewest-swaps score in an AI-assisted word game
author: Fantastic-Wrap-5176
selftext:
We built Word Seesaw, a free browser puzzle where you swap letter tiles until each row answers its clue. Codex helped write the game and its tests, and we used AI to draft puzzles and create artwork.



A tricky part was scoring boards with repeated letters. The same letter can come from several positions, and the first swap that fixes a tile isn’t always on the shortest path. Our solver tries the misplaced copies that can fix the first wrong tile and caches the resulting boards. To check the result independently, we compared it with an exhaustive search on small boards, including one with two copies each of A, B and C. The player-facing score comes from those swap rules, with the server replaying the submitted moves.



Try a daily board at https://wordseesaw.com/. If you’ve built a puzzle with an optimal score, how do you test the generator and explain the target so players trust it?
